sao-miguel-castelo.name: Church of São Miguel do Castelo
sao-miguel-castelo.short: A 13th-century Romanesque chapel by the castle where, legend says, Afonso Henriques was baptised
sao-miguel-castelo.long: The Collegiate of Oliveira built this small granite church, and Archbishop Silvestre Godinho of Braga consecrated it around 1239. Legend holds that the first King of Portugal was baptised in its font, although the church is a full century younger than the king. The floor is paved with the tomb slabs of knights. By the 1870s the church lay in ruins; the Martins Sarmento Society saved it.
sao-miguel-castelo.history:
The church is first mentioned in 1216, in a document of the collegiate of Guimarães. The canons built it in the middle of a quarrel with the Archbishop of Braga; the church went up against his will, which may explain its plainness: blank walls, slit windows, a single nave and a rectangular chancel. The inquiries of King Afonso III name the stonemason Garcia Petrarius. Archbishop Silvestre Godinho consecrated the church around 1239. That is late for Romanesque, and the details already hint at Gothic.

Legend ties the chapel to Afonso Henriques. To the left of the entrance stands a plain round granite font behind an iron gate, and beside it a stone with an inscription saying the future king was baptised in it in 1106. Historians do not believe it: the church was built a century later. But the legend outlived the centuries, and 19th-century Romantic nationalism made it stronger.

The floor is paved with granite slabs, many of them tombstones carved with the names and marks of knights. A frieze of interlaced ribbons decorates the triumphal arch. On the north façade, on either side of the door, are two arcosolia, burial niches, one of them with a carved archivolt.

In 1795 the prior of the collegiate replaced the arch between nave and chancel. By 1870 the church had ceased to be a parish church and stood in ruins. A commission of townspeople from the Martins Sarmento Society restored it in 1874–1880 and put the original arch back in place. On 16 June 1910 the church was listed as a National Monument together with the castle and the Dukes’ Palace. In 1936 a later belfry was taken off the façade, in 1939 the roof and doors were renewed, and in 1957 the landscape architect Viana Barreto laid out the ground around it.
facts: First mentioned in 1216 and consecrated around 1239.
A stone by the font claims Afonso Henriques was baptised here in 1106.
The floor is paved with the tomb slabs of medieval knights.
The Martins Sarmento Society rebuilt the ruin in 1874–1880.
sao-miguel-castelo.tip: The chapel stands on the “sacred hill” between the castle and the Dukes’ Palace, two minutes’ walk from either. It is dim inside: let your eyes adjust, then look at the floor slabs and the font to the left of the door. The terrace in front of the church has the best view of the castle.
